subject: Post-call action plan: competitive evaluation & observability tests
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-ml.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: inference platform comparison & observability concerns

Jordan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed action items so we can move to a side-by-side test next week.

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary goals: reduce per-token cost by 25-40% vs current provider, maintain p50 latency <50ms for short prompts, and preserve end-to-end traceability for troubleshooting.
- Observability must include per-request traces, request->model mapping, token-level cost breakdown, and retention of audit logs for 90 days.
- Your infra team wants a reproducible latency/throughput run (100 rps sustained for 5 minutes, plus a p95 spike test) and a demo of tracing continuity when we inject a failure.

Where Redwood shows differentiation (short list):
- Unified API that keeps the same SDK & tooling across hosted/dedicated/private deployments (reduces integration work).
- Built-in prefix/KV caching and autopipelining for conversational workloads — measurable cost reduction without extra engineering.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route/key dashboards, and native integrations with Datadog/Lightstep.

Proposed next steps (please confirm who owns each on your side):
1) Provide a short test dataset (50 representative prompts + 20 long-form prompts) and a test account with restricted API keys. Deadline: EOD Tue 5/12.
2) Redwood to run three tests: latency/throughput side-by-side vs CloudLabs and HyperscalerX; trace continuity failure injection; billing/token breakdown export. Deliverables: raw traces, latency histograms, cost delta report. ETA: week of 5/18.
3) Joint call to review results and remediation items. Proposed time: 30–45m on 5/20.
4) Security/questionnaire items — your SOC/infra asked for a short list of artifacts (SOC2 scope, logging retention, KMS usage). We attached a telemetry checklist and a lightweight competitive matrix to speed the legal/infosec review.

Attachments: competitive-matrix-v1.csv, postcall-telemetry-checklist.pdf

One logistics note: do you need an NDA before we touch any PII or internal traces? If yes, send the countersigned version and we'll expedite.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internally and assign test owners once you confirm the dataset and keys.

--
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-ml.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: inference platform comparison & observability concerns

Thanks Karthik — that recap is perfect.

We can share a scoped test key and the sample prompts. One ask: can Redwood sign our standard NDA? Also, for the latency/throughput run we want to include a burst test (p99) to see throttling behavior; please include that in the plan.

Attached is a temporary S3 link with anonymized traces from our current provider (s3://acme-ml/shared/anonymized-traces-2026-04). Please access with the temporary creds in the doc link I’ll DM to you.

I’ll loop in our infra lead Miguel if you need deep sys-level access during the run.

Jordan Lee
Head of ML Platforms | Acme ML
jordan.lee@acme-ml.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: test plan owners + checklist (fwd of Jordan)

Karthik — forwarding Jordan’s note and proposing owners so we can move fast: 
- Test orchestration & scripts: Monica Patel (me) — create infra in sandbox + runner.
- A/B control harness (compare CloudLabs/HyperscalerX/Redwood): Laura Bennett — implement traffic splitter and metric collectors.
- Observability & tracing validation: Karthik — verify trace continuity, token cost export, Datadog integration.

Key test items (expanded):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 across short (<=64 tokens) and long (>=512 tokens) prompts.
- Throughput: sustained 100 rps for 5m, 1m burst at 500 rps, record queueing/backpressure.
- Trace continuity: correlate application trace -> network -> model inference; inject a 500ms kernel delay to confirm span reconnection.
- Cost export: per-request token breakdown CSV, and simulated projected monthly bill for baseline workload.
- Security: verify logs do not contain raw PII; confirm KMS usage for model keys.

Link to shared test doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-ops-plan

I’ll draft the scripts this week. Karthik, once Jordan confirms the NDA and gives keys, I’ll kick off the sandbox build. Laura, can you estimate how long the A/B harness will take to stand up?

Date: 2026-05-14T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: inference platform comparison & observability concerns — next steps and schedule

Jordan / Miguel — thanks for the fast turnaround and the S3 pointer. We don’t need an NDA for the scoped, anonymized traces you already shared, but we will sign the NDA if you’d like us to review any non-anonymized or business-critical logs. Please send the countersigned copy if preferred.

Confirmed plan and timeline: 
- 5/12: Acme provides dataset + scoped API key (status: pending from Jordan).
- 5/15: Redwood completes sandbox infra and A/B harness (Monica/Laura).
- Week of 5/18: Execute tests (latency/throughput/burst/trace-injection). Deliver raw traces, latency histograms, and cost delta report within 48h of test completion.
- 5/20 or 5/21: Results review call (30–45m) — please confirm preferred slot.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Jordan: share test dataset + confirm NDA preference (due 5/12).
- Miguel: provide any infra allowlist or IPs for sandbox access (due 5/14).
- Monica: build runner and test scripts (due 5/15).
- Laura: implement A/B harness and dashboards (due 5/15).
- Karthik: run tracing validation and produce cost breakdown (deliverable after tests).

If that looks good, we’ll schedule the dry-run on 5/17 for our internal check and aim to run the customer-facing tests starting 5/18.

Thanks all — excited to show where Redwood can move the needle on both cost and operational visibility.

Best,

--
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
